actor: Unknown Carbonato botnet operators (ThreatDown assesses them as Costa Rica-based; no known cluster)

points.label: Costa Rica (assessed operator location, per ThreatDown)

impact: Per ThreatDown: hosts with exposed Docker APIs taken over through privileged containers, kept persistent and used for cryptocurrency mining, with a Hermes agent installed as an operator-tasked post-compromise tool directed at AI API keys and other credentials. Infection counts and stolen data are not reported. On 2026-09-03 six of seven known registries, the phishing sites, the CDN and the crew's LLM gateway were online.
mitigations: ThreatDown advises never exposing the Docker daemon API to the network and requiring authentication on every container registry.
Do not blocklist hermes-agent, which has legitimate users; hunt for its abuse instead, such as a persona file naming GH0ST, a CARBONATO_API_KEY setting or unexplained Telegram traffic from servers.

Check for the persistence kit (hidden watchdog binaries, disguised kernel-thread process names, a miner posing as a system service, unexpected immutable files) and for deterministic reverse SSH tunnels.
Treat AI API keys like bank credentials: inventory where they live, rotate them and monitor their usage.
name: Carbonato botnet installs a Hermes agent persona on hijacked Docker hosts as an operator interface prioritising AI API key theft

sources.title: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent
New Carbonato malware uses AI agents to hijack exposed Docker hosts

summary: ThreatDown (Malwarebytes) reported on 2026-09-22 the Carbonato botnet, found through an unauthenticated Docker registry that had been publicly exposed since May 2026 and held 59 repositories and 4.3 GB of image data spanning October 2024 to August 2026, alongside a separate trojanized cryptocurrency-wallet operation. The botnet compromises hosts whose Docker API is exposed without authentication, uses a privileged container to run commands on the host, opens a reverse SSH tunnel, installs layered persistence and a cryptocurrency miner, and spreads worm-like by scanning neighbouring networks every five minutes. On each host it installs the unmodified open-source Hermes Agent framework and overwrites the agent's persona file with a 39-line prompt naming it "GH0ST", disclaiming ethical limits and ranking AI provider API keys from 14 providers as the top loot, ahead of SSH credentials, tokens and databases. Operators send tasks over Telegram; the model, reached through the crew's own LLM gateway, interprets each task, writes and runs terminal commands on the victim and reports back. ThreatDown states that target selection, persistence and spreading are handled by scripts and that the model is absent from the propagation phase. It does not report how many hosts were infected or what the agent actually collected. ThreatDown assesses the operators as Costa Rica-based on linguistic, timezone, Telegram-handle and network signals, and could not link them to a known cluster.
